fun_facts: Wahoo are among the fastest-growing fish in the ocean: in their first year, some individuals pack on more than 3 millimetres of length a day, a growth rate matched by almost nothing else in the sea except mahi-mahi and striped marlin.

The much-repeated claim that a wahoo can hit 60 mph has never actually been measured; the one rigorous speed trial on record clocked a hooked wahoo at 48 mph in its first ten seconds of running, still startlingly fast, just not the number the fish is famous for.

A wahoo doesn't swallow prey whole the way many of its relatives do: its jaw carries a single row of triangular, razor-serrated teeth built for slicing baitfish into pieces first, which is also why an unhooked wahoo boatside is handled with real caution.

measures.label: Fork length
measures.help: Tip of the snout to the fork of the tail, measured in a straight line.

vocabs.label: Sex
vocabs.help: Wahoo cannot be sexed externally in the field; unknown is the normal answer.

not_taggable.reason: a fish in poor condition or bleeding is unlikely to survive release, so tagging it wastes the tag and the reward
